subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 35-year-old woman has had difficulty sleeping, irritability, and tearfulness for the past 2 months. These symptoms began about 6 weeks after her divorce, which she describes as a major life stressor. She continues to work and care for her children. Her symptoms do not meet criteria for major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder, and no life-threatening event occurred.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Adjustment disorder is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms such as anxiety and outbursts occurring within 3 months of an identifiable psychosocial stressor, lasting less than 6 months once the stressor has ended, and not meeting criteria for another psychiatric illness. A divorce is a classic psychosocial stressor and need not be life-threatening. CBT is first-line treatment, with antidepressants or anxiolytics considered in some cases.

explanation_incorrect.A: PTSD requires exposure to a life-threatening event such as serious injury or sexual assault followed by the HARD symptom clusters lasting more than 1 month; a divorce is a psychosocial stressor rather than a life-threatening trauma.
explanation_incorrect.B: Major depressive disorder requires at least five of nine symptoms for at least 2 weeks including depressed mood or anhedonia; her symptoms are tied to the stressor and do not meet full criteria.
explanation_incorrect.D: Acute stress disorder follows a traumatic event and lasts from 3 days to 1 month; this case involves a non-life-threatening stressor with a 2-month symptom course.
explanation_incorrect.E: Generalized anxiety disorder requires excessive worry about multiple aspects of daily life for most days over at least 6 months with at least three associated symptoms, which is not present here.

educationalObjective: Adjustment disorder follows an identifiable psychosocial stressor within 3 months, lasts under 6 months after the stressor ends, and does not meet criteria for another disorder.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 27-year-old man was in a serious car collision 6 weeks ago in which his friend was killed. Since the accident he has had recurrent nightmares and intrusive images of the crash, avoids driving, feels detached from others, and startles easily. He reports that these symptoms have been present continuously since the event. He has no prior psychiatric history.
question: Which of the following best characterizes his condition based on symptom duration?

options.text: Acute stress disorder, because symptoms began within 3 days of the event
PTSD, because symptoms have persisted for more than 1 month
Adjustment disorder, because symptoms followed an identifiable stressor
Brief psychotic disorder, because symptoms are stress-related
A normal stress reaction, because symptoms are time-limited

explanation_correct: PTSD follows a life-threatening event and produces persistent hyperarousal, avoidance, intrusive re-experiencing, and changes in cognition or mood with distress lasting more than 1 month. This man has nightmares and intrusive images, avoidance of driving, detachment, and hyperarousal lasting 6 weeks. The duration beyond 1 month distinguishes PTSD from acute stress disorder, which lasts 3 days to 1 month and is treated with CBT.

explanation_incorrect.A: Acute stress disorder lasts from 3 days up to 1 month; symptoms persisting for 6 weeks exceed that window and instead meet the duration criterion for PTSD.
explanation_incorrect.C: Adjustment disorder follows a non-life-threatening psychosocial stressor and lasts less than 6 months; a fatal collision with intrusive re-experiencing and hyperarousal is a life-threatening trauma better captured by PTSD.
explanation_incorrect.D: Brief psychotic disorder involves at least one positive psychotic symptom such as hallucinations, delusions, or disorganized speech lasting 1 day to 1 month; he has no psychotic symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.E: Although acute stress reactions can be time-limited, symptoms lasting more than 1 month with significant impairment meet criteria for PTSD and warrant treatment with CBT, SSRIs, or venlafaxine.

educationalObjective: Trauma-related symptoms lasting more than 1 month meet criteria for PTSD, whereas acute stress disorder lasts 3 days to 1 month.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 34-year-old woman was sexually assaulted 3 months ago. She reports difficulty falling asleep, an exaggerated startle response, and irritability. She avoids the street where the assault occurred and has intrusive flashbacks of the event. She also describes persistent fear and horror and a sense of detachment from other people.
question: Which of the following symptom clusters, taken together, best supports the diagnosis of PTSD in this patient?

options.text: Depressed mood, anhedonia, and guilt only
Palpitations, choking, and fear of dying during discrete attacks
Excessive worry about work and health for most days over 6 months
Hyperarousal, avoidance, intrusive re-experiencing, and negative changes in cognition and mood
Preoccupation with having a serious illness despite repeated reassurance

explanation_correct: PTSD is characterized by the HARD features: Hyperarousal, Avoidance of associated stimuli, intrusive Re-experiencing of the event, and Distress with changes in cognition or mood, lasting more than 1 month. This patient has all four clusters. First-line treatment is CBT, SSRIs, and venlafaxine, and prazosin can be added to reduce nightmares.

explanation_incorrect.A: Depressed mood, anhedonia, and guilt are features of major depressive disorder; depression can co-occur with PTSD, but this cluster alone does not capture the trauma-specific HARD features.
explanation_incorrect.B: Palpitations, choking, and fear of dying during discrete attacks describe panic attacks in panic disorder, not the persistent trauma-related syndrome of PTSD.
explanation_incorrect.C: Excessive worry about multiple domains for at least 6 months describes generalized anxiety disorder, not a syndrome with re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal after a trauma.
explanation_incorrect.E: Preoccupation with having a serious illness despite reassurance describes illness anxiety disorder, which lacks the re-experiencing and avoidance seen in PTSD.

educationalObjective: PTSD is defined by hyperarousal, avoidance, re-experiencing, and negative cognitive or mood changes lasting more than 1 month after a life-threatening event.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 42-year-old veteran with PTSD continues to have frequent distressing nightmares about combat despite participating in trauma-focused therapy. His physician is considering adding a medication specifically to reduce the nightmares.
question: Which of the following medications is most appropriate for reducing trauma-related nightmares in this patient?
explanation_correct: Prazosin is an alpha-1 antagonist that can reduce nightmares associated with PTSD. Overall first-line treatment for PTSD includes CBT, SSRIs, and venlafaxine, with prazosin added for persistent nightmares. It should not be confused with the treatment of acute stress disorder, for which pharmacotherapy is usually not indicated.

explanation_incorrect.B: Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic used for psychotic disorders and acute agitation, not the agent used specifically to reduce PTSD nightmares.
explanation_incorrect.C: Lorazepam is a benzodiazepine; benzodiazepines are generally not recommended in PTSD because of poor efficacy for core symptoms and risk of dependence.
explanation_incorrect.D: Methylphenidate is a stimulant used for ADHD and has no established role in reducing trauma-related nightmares.
explanation_incorrect.E: Lithium is a mood stabilizer used in bipolar disorder and is not used for nightmares in PTSD.

educationalObjective: Prazosin is used to reduce trauma-related nightmares in PTSD, while CBT, SSRIs, and venlafaxine are first-line for the disorder overall.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 29-year-old woman was diagnosed with PTSD after a sexual assault 2 months ago. She and her physician are discussing first-line treatment, and she asks which interventions have the strongest support for her condition.
question: Which of the following is considered first-line treatment for PTSD?
explanation_correct: First-line treatment for PTSD consists of CBT, SSRIs, and venlafaxine. Prazosin can be added specifically for nightmares. In contrast, acute stress disorder is treated with CBT, and pharmacotherapy is usually not indicated for it.

explanation_incorrect.A: Benzodiazepines are not recommended as first-line treatment for PTSD and may be associated with worse outcomes or dependence.
explanation_incorrect.B: Typical antipsychotics are used for psychotic disorders, not as first-line therapy for PTSD.
explanation_incorrect.C: Tricyclic antidepressants are not first-line for PTSD; SSRIs and venlafaxine are the preferred pharmacologic options.
explanation_incorrect.D: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors can be effective for some anxiety and depressive disorders but are not first-line for PTSD because of their adverse-effect and interaction burden.

educationalObjective: First-line PTSD treatment is CBT, an SSRI, or venlafaxine, with prazosin reserved for nightmares.
